slides.title: An Introduction to Troubleshooting Troubleshooting Troubleshooting is a form of problem solving, often applied to repair
slides.body:
Troubleshooting is a form of problem solving, often applied to repair failed
products or processes.
o It is a logical, systematic search for the root cause of a problem to solve it.
o Determining the most likely cause is a process of elimination, eliminating potential
causes of a problem.
o Finally, troubleshooting requires confirmation that the solution restores the product or
process to its working state.

to solve a
problem I’d spend

thinking about

slides.title: A basic principle in troubleshooting is to start from the simplest and most probable possible problems first. This means
slides.body:
This means to use the Occam’s razor.
Occam's razor is the problem-solving principle that states "Entities should not be
multiplied without necessity." The idea is attributed to English Franciscan friar William
of Ockham (c. 1287–1347), a scholastic philosopher and theologian. It is sometimes
paraphrased by a statement like "The simplest solution is most likely the right
one."

slides.title: Troubleshooting Basic Principles
slides.body:
Define the Issue
- an incorrect assessment could affect all subsequent activity
o Cartesio’s Method:
- Never accept anything as true if you don't have specific evidence (Doubt)
- This rule helps you not to fall victim to solving the problem "on the spot": no matter how tempting many of
us are, you should never jump to conclusions!
- Divide the problem into easy-to-solve problems (Simplification)
- Reducing the problem into smaller parts allows you to narrow down the individual difficulties and find a
solution consistent with the general problem for each individual aspect.
- Start solving the simpler things and then move on to the more complex ones (Focus)
- We focus on the aspects that are easier to solve, leaving the most difficult ones for last
- Do not omit anything from your considerations (Completeness)
- critically examines all aspects and related sub-problems

slides.title: General advices o Base your theory on facts as much as possible. o A theory is good if you can test it, even if it’s the
slides.body:
o A theory is good if you can test it, even if it’s the wrong one.
o Don’t be afraid of being wrong: it is normal during the process and the
environment around you should accept it.
o If you are wrong simply discard your theory and think about another.
o If you are not able to get the solution by yourself, then help someone else to
get it: it is not important who will find the solution but to get the solution itself
in a reasonable amount of time. Always share your ideas with people
involved into the same issue.

o Carefully examine available data: don’t wait for “perfect” data because all

slides.body:
Sample Case1 Troubleshooting
It the battery is drained, its work is adversely
affected.
However, it’s much worse if the situation occurs
repeatedly. In this case, it is worth considering
why your “iron horse” behaves in such a way. In
fact, some of major causes are as follows:
- wearing of the battery;
- mismatch of the charge / discharge ratio when
charging from the alternator;
- alternator failure;
- starter malfunction / poor operation;
- external leakage currents.

slides.title: Sample Case1 Troubleshooting
slides.body:
Measuring Leakage Current
Before you start testing, you need to undertake preparatory work.
First of all, leave the hood open and turn off all current consumers, e.g., a car radio, exterior and interior
lights, then remove the key from the ignition lock and close the door. Please remember that when you
measure with a multimeter, the battery will be switching on and off, so the central lock may be triggered.
It is therefore better to leave the windows open to secure access to the car.
To make measurements, we’ll need:
o a multimeter with a DC measuring range not less than 10 A
o Alligator test clips (for more convenient connection);
o an 8 or 10 box or open end wrench (needs to be picked for a vehicle);
o work gloves.
It is quite convenient to measure leakage current clamp meters – no need to disconnect anything, just
crimp the wire and make measurements. Clamp meters’ disadvantage is that they are not too precise and
can capture parasitic currents. Still, by resetting with the "Zero" button you can achieve accurate and
precise results.
You need to crimp either a positive or a negative cable with all the wires connected to one of the
terminals (if any). The only important point is that clamp meters should measure DC current. As a rule,
their price is much higher if compared to regular clamp meters that measure only AC.

slides.title: Sample Case1 Troubleshooting
slides.body:
Checking Relays and Fuses
The fuse service box and relay box are located under the hood. It is also possible to
place another block (box) in the passenger compartment near the dashboard, under
the rear seat, and also in the boot. We can search for a potential consumer of excess
current in the following way:
o connect the multimeter in the same way you connect it when measuring leakage
current;
o remove each fuse one after another and insert them back in place, noting whether
the current value on the multimeter display changes;
o if you find a significant (yet permissible) decrease, consult the vehicle technical
documentation to learn what this fuse is responsible for and proceed to the
detailed testing of devices which work with the fuse.
o Imagine you’ve checked all fuses, but there is still leakage current.
In this case, you need to check the devices not protected by fuses. These are:
o alternator;
o starter.
1. Fuse and relay box
2. Front PDC
